expected_evidence: Geological: a discrete sedimentary marker horizon at ~12,800-12,900 cal BP (the 'Younger Dryas Boundary' layer) across North American sites containing platinum/iridium anomalies, magnetic microspherules, nanodiamonds, and carbon-rich 'black mat' layers interpreted as impact ejecta fallout

Astronomical: independent corroborating signals such as a confirmed impact crater or crater field, cosmic-spherule chemistry consistent with extraterrestrial/cometary origin, or contemporaneous airburst debris fields; absence of a confirmed crater is a major gap in the real record

Material/archaeological: abrupt discontinuity or thinning in Clovis-culture artifact density immediately above the proposed ejecta layer, scorched/burned megafaunal bone beds, and reduced large-mammal kill sites postdating the horizon

Genetic: population bottleneck or extinction signatures in megafaunal (mammoth, horse, camelid, etc.) mitochondrial/nuclear DNA dated to ~12,800-11,700 BP, and possible human population bottleneck signals in ancient North American genomes

Model-prior (unverified, from training knowledge, not the evidence text): this maps onto the actively published and contested 'Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis' (Firestone et al. 2007 and successors), for which dozens of sites have reported spherules/nanodiamonds, but multiple independent replication studies (Pigati, Holliday, Boslough, Daulton, Surovell and others) failed to reproduce key markers, disputed nanodiamond identification as artifacts, and no impact crater has been confirmed - so the hypothesis remains scientifically unresolved/largely rejected in mainstream literature rather than confirmed
response.rationale: The interval (-19050 to -9050) spans Upper Paleolithic through Younger Dryas into earliest Holocene, periods where geological (0.60-0.65) and astronomical (0.65-0.70) detectability are comparatively high because ejecta layers, spherules, and geochemical anomalies are robust, long-lived physical signals that survive burial in sediment for tens of thousands of years and are actively sought by researchers. This is why a real, if contested, body of published evidence exists for the Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis - the mechanism is testable and has been tested. However, material (archaeological, ~0.35-0.45) and genetic (~0.25-0.35) evidence for the causal 'corroboration' link to megafaunal extinction specifically are weaker and more equivocal, since taphonomic loss, poor preservation of soft tissue/DNA over 10,000+ years, and confounding extinction drivers (climate change, human overhunting) degrade the diagnostic value of what does survive. Textual (0.0-0.02) and oral_tradition (0.1) evidence are essentially unavailable given the absence of writing and the extreme time depth for oral transmission fidelity. Given this mix, I set an overall detectability adjustment of 0.55, weighted toward the higher geological/astronomical channels since those are the primary evidentiary tests of an impact-ejecta mechanism, while discounting for the weaker material/genetic corroboration and near-zero textual/oral channels. Because detectability is only moderate-to-good rather than high, and because the real-world literature shows genuine, unresolved scientific controversy over replication of the key markers (a fact I hold as model-prior, not from the provided evidence text), an absence of clean, converging evidence should be read as reflecting this detectability ceiling and ongoing methodological dispute rather than as proof the hypothesis is false.
